1.title: Responding in Defender XDR (2): Identities, Entra ID Protection and Defender for Identity
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Responding in Defender X D R (two): Identities, Entra I D Protection and Defender for Identity. It covers the exam area two. Respond to security incidents. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Investigate and remediate compromised identities that are identified by Microsoft Entra I D. Investigate and remediate security alerts from Microsoft Defender for Identity. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Respond to security incidents (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Microsoft Entra ID Protection
1.text: Microsoft Entra I D Protection. Entra I D Protection detects risky sign-ins and risky users in the cloud. Path: Entra admin center, then Protection, then Identity Protection. Full access needs Microsoft Entra I D P two.

1.title: Microsoft Entra ID Protection, continued
1.text: Microsoft Entra I D Protection. The figure shows this: Risk detections feed risky sign-ins and risky users, which risk-based policies and analysts remediate.

1.title: Microsoft Entra ID Protection, continued
1.text: Microsoft Entra I D Protection. Risk detections. Each detection (for example leaked credentials, atypical travel). Risky sign-ins. Sign-ins with a sign-in risk. Risky users. Users with user risk (a user has risky sign-ins or detections). Risk levels: Low, Medium, High. Leaked credentials is always High. Detections are real-time (R T) or offline (Off). Leaked credentials. User risk, offline. Anomalous token, Attacker in the middle. Token theft; no automatic remediation. Atypical travel, Anonymous I P address, Password spray, Unfamiliar sign-in properties. Sign-in risk. Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (P R T). User risk (with Defender for Endpoint).

1.title: Remediating risk
1.text: Remediating risk. Dismiss user risk or dismiss sign-in. State becomes Dismissed (needs Security Operator). Confirm user compromised. State becomes Confirmed compromised; follow with password change, revoke tokens, block. Reset password (or temporary password). State becomes Remediated (needs Security Operator plus User Administrator). Require password change (from a policy). User does M F A, then a secure password change; Remediated. Self-remediation. M F A clears sign-in risk; a secure password change clears user risk.

1.title: Remediating risk, continued
1.text: Remediating risk. Security Reader. View reports only. Security Operator. View, dismiss, confirm safe or compromised; no policy changes. Security Administrator. Full Identity Protection access (cannot reset passwords). User Administrator. Reset passwords only. Conditional Access Administrator. Creates Conditional Access policies with risk conditions.

1.title: Risk-based Conditional Access
1.text: Risk-based Conditional Access. User risk policy. Condition: User risk equals High (recommended). Grant: Require risk remediation (older name Require password change). Sign-in risk policy. Condition: Medium and High. Grant: Require authentication strength: Multifactor authentication; sign-in frequency Every time. Do not combine user risk and sign-in risk in one policy. Start in Report-only mode. The legacy Identity Protection risk policies retire on October one, twenty twenty-six; use Conditional Access. Exam tip: User risk to password change. Sign-in risk to M F A. Token-theft detections (anomalous token, attacker in the middle) are not auto-remediated: an analyst revokes sessions and tokens.

1.title: Microsoft Defender for Identity
1.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity. Defender for Identity protects on-premises Active Directory (and hybrid identities) with sensors on domain controllers. Version three point x. Windows Server twenty nineteen or later; onboarded through Defender for Endpoint; uses the local system account; no V P N (virtual private network) integration or sys log. Version two point x. Windows Server twenty sixteen or earlier; supports V P N integration and sys log; uses a G M S A.

1.title: Microsoft Defender for Identity, continued
1.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity. Install on all domain controllers (including read-only), and on A D F S, A D C S and Entra Connect servers that are not domain controllers. Both versions can run together. Reconnaissance. Account enumeration (L D A P), honeytoken queried. Compromised credentials. Brute force (Kerberos, N T L M). Lateral movement. Pass-the-hash identity theft. Domain dominance. D C sync, D C shadow, Golden Ticket.

1.title: Microsoft Defender for Identity, continued
1.text: Microsoft Defender for Identity. Severity: High, Medium, Low. Some alerts have learning periods (brute force one week, L D A P (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) recon fifteen days). Tuning in the Defender format uses alert tuning rules (Module one). Exam tip: Defender for Identity covers on-premises Active Directory; Entra I D Protection covers cloud sign-ins. Match the identity source in the scenario to the product.

1.title: Identity response actions
1.text: Identity response actions. Path: Assets, then Identities (identity inventory), advanced hunting, or the Action center. You need a custom unified R back role with Response (manage). Disable. Active Directory, Entra, Okta and other connected sources; does not delete the profile. Enable. Reverses disable. Revoke session. Entra and Okta. Mark as compromised. Entra only; needs Global Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Operator or sock Identity Responder. Force password change. Forces a new password at next sign-in.

1.title: Identity response actions, continued
1.text: Identity response actions. On-premises actions run on the domain controller sensor under the local system account (required for version three.x); Entra actions run through the managed app Microsoft Defender for Identity. Identity inventory (Assets, then Identities) shows human and non-human identities, a risk score zero to one hundred, and whether the identity is on-premises, cloud-only or hybrid. Exam tip: Disable equals A D account. Mark as compromised equals Entra only. Revoke session equals Entra and Okta.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. The sock wants users with a High user risk, for example from leaked credentials, to change their passwords automatically at the next sign-in. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A user risk Conditional Access policy that requires risk remediation. A user risk policy with the User risk condition set to High and the risk remediation (password change) grant fixes user risk.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Sign-ins with medium or high sign-in risk must be challenged without forcing a password change. Which policy fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A sign-in risk policy that requires multifactor authentication. Sign-in risk is remediated with M F A, in a separate sign-in risk policy.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An analyst must dismiss false risk detections and confirm users as compromised, but must not change Conditional Access or reset passwords. Which role fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Security Operator, which can dismiss risk and confirm compromise. Security Operator can view, dismiss and confirm; it cannot change policies or reset passwords.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Defender for Identity raises a D C sync alert for an on-premises account. The analyst wants to stop the account immediately in Active Directory. Which action should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Disable, run through the sensor on the domain controller. Disable applies to Active Directory accounts and runs on the sensor; Mark as compromised is Entra only.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A domain controller runs Windows Server twenty sixteen. Which Defender for Identity sensor version should be deployed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Version two point x, which supports Windows Server twenty sixteen or earlier. Version three point x needs Windows Server twenty nineteen or later; version two point x supports older servers.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A detection named Attacker in the middle raised a user to High risk. What is true about remediation? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: It is not auto-remediated; the analyst must revoke sessions and tokens. Token-theft detections are not auto-remediated, so tokens and sessions must be revoked.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which license gives full Entra I D Protection access? Answer: Microsoft Entra I D P two. Question two. What is the risk level of leaked credentials? Answer: Always High. Question three. Which action is Entra only? Answer: Mark as compromised.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which sensor needs Windows Server twenty nineteen or later? Answer: Version three point x. Question five. Where is the identity inventory? Answer: Assets, then Identities. Question six. When do legacy Identity Protection risk policies retire? Answer: October one, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Reports: risk detections, risky sign-ins, risky users. Policies: user risk High to password change; sign-in risk Medium and High to M F A. Roles: Reader views, Operator dismisses and confirms, Administrator configures, User Administrator resets. Sensors: version three.x Server twenty nineteen plus, local system; version two.x older, G M S A. Actions: Disable, Enable, Revoke session, Mark as compromised, Force password change. Permission: custom unified R back with Response (manage). If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
